newsitem.title: USA: Westvaco sees stronger order patterns.
newsitem.headline: Westvaco sees stronger order patterns.

text.p: Westvaco Corp Chairman and Chief Executive John Luke said Tuesday the company has begun to see signs of stronger order patterns for paper, an indication the market's downturn may not be as severe as it was in the early 1990s.
Luke said those indications have begun cropping up in the early stages of the fourth quarter ending October 31.
"When this downturn began, we stated that we did not expect our markets to dip into a lengthy slide such as we experienced in the early 1990s," he said in a statement. "That remains our view."

Luke said demand has increased gradually throughout the year, but "pressure on pricing, particularly for unbleached commodity products and certain coated printing paper grades, has continued through the third quarter."
Luke said the fourth quarter is normally the company's strongest period.

Westvaco reported net income of $43.6 million, or $0.43 per share, on revenues of $757.7 million for its third quarter ended July 31 compared with net income of $77.6 million, or $0.77 per share, on revenues of $854.6 million in the same period in 1995.
